content:
**sdd/issue-229-c4/explore**

## Exploration: C4 (issue #229) — close the post-cutover transitional window

### Current State (grounded findings, file:line)

**D1 — dualWrite config machinery (HIGHEST PRIORITY)**
- Sole runtime read site: `brain/scripts/memory/backends/engram.mjs:176` — `if (_loadConfig(root)?.memory?.dualWrite === true) { await dualWriteRecords(...) }` inside `share()` (engram.mjs:153-179). No other read call site in the whole repo (migrate-v1.mjs never reads it).
- Config load: `brain/scripts/lib/brain-config.mjs` `loadBrainConfig()`/`ensureBrainConfig()`; migrations registry at `brain/core/config-migrations.mjs` (6 entries, ALL additive via `{defaults}`, none via custom `migrate()`). `memory.dualWrite` added at migration `0.6.0` (config-migrations.mjs:86-99), default `false`.
- `mergeDefaults()` (`brain/scripts/lib/installer.mjs:364-377`) can ONLY ADD missing keys — `if (!(key in out)) out[key] = defVal` — it structurally CANNOT remove a key. `migrateConfig()` (installer.mjs:422-442) only ever calls `mergeDefaults` or a custom `migrate(config, {mergeDefaults})` fn; every one of the 6 existing migrations uses the `defaults` (pure-additive) form. Zero precedent for a destructive/removal migration anywhere in the codebase.
- Real repo's own `brain.config.json` (repo root) has `"memory":{"dualWrite":true}` but `"schemaVersion":"0.3.0"` — STALE relative to the 0.6.0 migration that key belongs to. This proves `dualWrite:true` was set here by a MANUAL edit (the C2b-2 runbook's human keystroke), NOT via `migrateConfig`/`brain-upgrade.mjs`. `brain-upgrade.mjs` (lines 160-184) is the only code path that ever runs `migrateConfig`, and it is a manual/opt-in consumer command, not something CI or `npm test` runs against this repo's own config.
- Consequence for the decision: whichever mechanism C4 picks, THIS repo's own `brain.config.json` still needs a manual edit to actually remove/ignore the key locally — `config-migrations.mjs` changes only affect (a) fresh installs (`buildDefaultConfig()`, brain-config.mjs:119-142) and (b) downstream consumers who run `brain-upgrade`.

**D2 — pull/import path**
- `importMemory()` (engram.mjs:477-480) and `pullMemory()` (engram.mjs:513-533) are 100% chunk-based today: `execFileSync(engram, ["sync", "--import"])` — an opaque call into the engram binary that hydrates local engram from `.memory/chunks/*.jsonl.gz`.
- `importRecord()` (`brain/scripts/memory/lib/engram-import.mjs:56-74`, shipped in C2b-1) is a PURE transform (record → engram observation shape) that is currently exercised ONLY by `engram-import.test.mjs` — it is NOT wired into `importMemory`/`pullMemory`/CLI `pull`/`import` at all. Confirmed via `engram.pull.test.mjs` (only mocked seams, no records path).
- Existing precedent for injecting a record into engram directly: `featureResume()`'s `_defaultEngramSave()` (engram.mjs:916-922) calls `execFileSync("engram", ["save", title, content, "--type", type, "--project", project, "--topic", topic])` — i.e. `engram save` is a real per-observation CLI verb already used elsewhere in this codebase. This is the natural mechanism to wire records-only import (read `.memory/records/*.jsonl` via `readRecordObservations`/`store.mjs`, transform via `importRecord()`, call `engram save` per record) instead of `engram sync --import` (chunks).
- `cli.mjs` VALID_OPS: `share|pull|import|index|reindex|migrate-v1|setup|feature-checkpoint|feature-resume` (cli.mjs:53-63); `pull`→`pullMemory`, `import`→`importMemory` via VERB_TO_EXPORT map (cli.mjs:210-215).

**D3/D4 — memory-gate chunks retirement**
- `brain/scripts/governance/run-check.mjs:7,10-14,34-35,85,91` — memory-gate currently unions `readChunkObservations(cwd)` (`brain/scripts/lib/chunk-reader.mjs:23-42`) and `readRecordObservations(cwd)` (`brain/scripts/memory/lib/store.mjs:151-176`). Comment explicitly: "Retire the chunks-path once it is fully decommissioned (tracked for C4/D1)." Both readers are TRANSITIONAL by their own doc comments.
- **Cutover finding 7 CONFIRMED**: `_defaultChangedChunkFiles` (`engram.mjs:352-372`) runs `git status --porcelain --- .memory/chunks`, then `.split("\n").map(l => l.slice(3).trim()).filter(p => p.endsWith(".jsonl.gz"))` — NO filter on the porcelain status prefix (e.g. `D `/` D` for deletions also end in `.jsonl.gz` and pass the filter). Every returned path is then fed to `scrubChunkFile()` (`brain/scripts/memory/lib/secret-scrub.mjs:104-115`), which does `readFileSync(chunkPath)` at line 105 with NO existence guard — a deleted chunk path → ENOENT throw. This is a live bug in `scrubMaterializedChunks()` (engram.mjs:388-402), which the first post-cutover `share()` that deletes any chunk (e.g. cutover moved chunks to `legacy/`) will trip. Must be fixed in or before C4.

**D1 (round-trip) — format.mjs / provenance.mjs**
- `brain/scripts/memory/lib/format.mjs`: `computeRecordId` (66-82, excludes `source` from hash per R3), `buildRecord` (99-107, R2 title fold).
- `brain/scripts/memory/lib/provenance.mjs`: `renderProvenance`/`parseProvenance` (123-140 / 65-103) — the §4 prose grammar, already referencing `sdd/memory-format/c4-roundtrip-equality` as its own acceptance criterion (provenance.mjs top comment + engram-import.mjs:9 + engram-import.test.mjs:4-7).
- Existing round-trip scaffolding: `engram-import.test.mjs` ALREADY has full id-equality property tests including the EXACT issue-without-source pin the user described (lines 46-60: `roundTripId(record)` = `computeRecordId(exportObservation(importRecord(record)).record)` must equal `record.id`; asserts re-exported `source` becomes `'issue #305'` while original `record.source === undefined` — inert because `source` is hash-excluded). This is SYNTHETIC-fixture only.
- Gap for C4 D1: NO round-trip test exists yet against REAL committed data. Real records live at `.memory/records/2026-06.jsonl` (135 `@legacy` records from the cutover migration, of ~275 total) and `.memory/records/2026-07.jsonl`. Precedent for a real-git-repo integration test style: `records-merge.integration.test.mjs` (builds temp repo, real git merge) — but that too uses synthetic records, not the actual committed store. C4 should add an integration test that reads the REAL `.memory/records/*.jsonl` (via `readRecordObservations`/`parseRecordLine`) and asserts `computeRecordId(exportObservation(importRecord(r)).record) === r.id` for every real record.

**D5 — openspec artifact convention**
`openspec/changes/issue-222-c2b2-cutover/` contains: `proposal.md`, `spec.md`, `tasks.md`, `checkpoint-report.md`, `design.md`, `runbook.md`. The phase-order gate (`brain/scripts/vcs/phase-order-check.mjs`) requires `proposal.md` (line 326), `design.md` (327), `spec.md` OR `specs/*/spec.md` (329, 294), and `tasks.md` with checked items — all 4 must exist for any dir with implementation code, else Rule C fails. `issue-229-c4/` must mirror at minimum proposal/spec/design/tasks.md.

### Affected Areas
- `brain/core/config-migrations.mjs` — dualWrite removal/deprecation mechanism
- `brain/scripts/lib/brain-config.mjs`, `brain/scripts/lib/installer.mjs` (mergeDefaults/migrateConfig) — additive-only constraint
- `brain/scripts/memory/backends/engram.mjs` — share()'s dualWrite gate (176), pullMemory/importMemory (477-533), _defaultChangedChunkFiles bug (352-372)
- `brain/scripts/memory/lib/engram-import.mjs` — importRecord(), unwired into CLI pull/import
- `brain/scripts/memory/lib/secret-scrub.mjs:104-115` — scrubChunkFile ENOENT risk on deleted paths
- `brain/scripts/governance/run-check.mjs`, `brain/scripts/lib/chunk-reader.mjs`, `brain/scripts/memory/lib/store.mjs` — memory-gate dual-source union to retire
- `brain/scripts/memory/lib/format.mjs`, `provenance.mjs`, `engram-import.test.mjs` — round-trip contract, needs real-data integration test
- `.memory/records/2026-06.jsonl`, `.memory/records/2026-07.jsonl` — real fixture data for D1's integration test

### Approaches — dualWrite removal (D1, the key decision)
1. **(a) schemaVersion-bump migration that REMOVES the key** — requires writing the FIRST-EVER non-additive `migrate(config, helpers)` function (all 6 existing migrations are pure `defaults`). Contradicts the file's own doctrine comment ("Migrations are ADDITIVE... NEVER overwrite... idempotent"). Also does not self-apply to THIS repo (own config already proven to need a manual edit regardless, since schemaVersion is stale at 0.3.0). Benefit: config is honestly clean going forward for downstream consumers running brain-upgrade.
   - Effort: Medium (new non-additive migration pattern + doctrine exception to justify + tests)
2. **(b) tolerate-and-ignore with deprecation warning** — delete the ONE read site (engram.mjs:176) or make it a no-op with a console.warn if `memory.dualWrite` is still present; leave the config key alone (or add a NEW additive migration that does nothing but document deprecation in a comment/description). Zero new migration mechanism needed, consistent with existing additive-only doctrine. Con: config key lingers forever in every consumer's file (minor clutter), and doesn't "close the window" as cleanly by the letter of D1's goal.
   - Effort: Low (single call-site change + optional warning)

### Recommendation
Favor **(b)**, with a twist: since dualWrite already flipped to `true` in production (this repo's `brain.config.json` confirms the real cutover happened), the code's job is simply to stop CONDITIONING on it — always dual-write is now just "the only write path" (records-only). The cleanest move is to delete the `if (dualWrite === true)` branch entirely and make `dualWriteRecords()` (or its replacement, unconditional record-write logic) run unconditionally in `share()`, then treat the config key as inert/deprecated (leave it in config-migrations.mjs history for provenance, optionally add a one-line description update noting "RETIRED at C4, no longer read"). This avoids inventing the repo's first destructive migration primitive for a key that has exactly one reader, while still fully "retiring" the gate from the code's perspective. If the team wants the config file itself to visibly shed the key for new installs, a narrow non-`defaults`-based migration entry could still be layered on later without blocking C4.

### Risks
- The `_defaultChangedChunkFiles` ENOENT bug (finding 7) is LIVE now that the real store has moved chunks to `legacy/` — any `memory:share` that also deletes a chunk will crash `scrubMaterializedChunks`. Should be fixed as part of D3/D4 or as a prerequisite hotfix.
- D2 (pull/import records-only) has NO existing wiring at all — it's greenfield, not a refactor. The engram binary's only documented per-observation write verb is `engram save` (used in featureResume); reusing that pattern for bulk records import needs a design decision on batching/performance for ~275+ records.
- D1's real-data round-trip test must handle the 135 `@legacy`-actor records from the cutover migration (source = "provenance unknown — migrated from engram chunk ...") as its dominant real-world case, not just synthetic pins.
- Removing/deprecating `dualWrite` while `run-check.mjs`'s memory-gate still unions both readers (D3/D4) means D1 and D4 are coupled — sequencing matters in tasks.md.

### Ready for Proposal
Yes — sufficient grounded evidence exists for all 5 deliverables to author design.md and drive strict TDD. Key open question for the proposal/design phase: confirm with @csrinaldi whether config-key removal (option a) is a value worth paying doctrine-exception cost for, or whether option (b)'s "stop reading it" is acceptable given the key already served its purpose.
